title: Mathematical Methods for Physicists
subject: Applied Mathematics
description: Essential mathematical tools for advanced physics. Focuses on vector spaces, differential equations, complex analysis, tensor analysis, and boundary value problems.
syllabus_topics: Vector spaces and curvilinear coordinate systems
Partial differential equations and boundary conditions
Introduction to tensor analysis and differential forms
Complex variables and contour integration
Green's functions and Sturm-Liouville theory
textbooks: Mathematical Methods for Physicists by George Arfken & Hans Weber
relevance: Provides the foundational tensor calculus and differential geometry mathematical tools needed to comprehend and formulate Einstein's Field Equations.

title: Advanced Electromagnetism
subject: Physics
description: A rigorous treatment of electrodynamics based on Maxwell's equations. Covers electrostatic and magnetostatic fields, electromagnetic waves, radiation, and relativistic electrodynamics.
syllabus_topics: Maxwell's equations in vacuum and matter
Electromagnetic wave propagation and waveguides
Potentials, gauge transformations (Lorenz & Coulomb gauges)
Radiation from moving charges and dipole radiation
Relativistic formulation of electrodynamics and field tensor F^uv
textbooks: Classical Electrodynamics by John David Jackson
relevance: Relativistic electrodynamics introduces four-vectors and the electromagnetic field tensor, serving as the bridge to Special Relativity and the study of ion wind propulsion (Biefeld-Brown).

title: Quantum Mechanics I
subject: Physics
description: Fundamental principles of quantum mechanics. Formulates the Schrodinger equation, wave functions, operators, angular momentum, spin, and perturbation theory.
syllabus_topics: The postulates of quantum mechanics and Hilbert spaces
One-dimensional problems (harmonic oscillator, potential wells)
Angular momentum and quantum mechanical spin
Three-dimensional systems and the hydrogen atom
Time-independent perturbation theory
textbooks: Introduction to Quantum Mechanics by David J. Griffiths
Principles of Quantum Mechanics by R. Shankar
relevance: Essential for understanding subatomic interactions, quantum fluctuations (Casimir effect), and the ultimate search for a unified Quantum Gravity theory.

title: Fluid Dynamics & Aerodynamics
subject: Aerospace Engineering
description: Governing equations of fluid motion. Focuses on inviscid and viscous flows, incompressible and compressible flow regimes, boundary layer theory, and aerodynamic forces.
syllabus_topics: Navier-Stokes equations derivation and conservation laws
Potential flow theory and lift generation
Viscous flow and laminar/turbulent boundary layers
One-dimensional compressible flow and shock waves
Introduction to computational fluid dynamics (CFD)
textbooks: Fundamentals of Aerodynamics by John D. Anderson
relevance: Provides the fluid mechanics frameworks needed to analyze ionized gas flow in EHD propulsion systems (lifters) and warp-bubble fluid analogies.

title: General Relativity & Gravitation
subject: Physics
description: A comprehensive introduction to Einstein's theory of gravitation. Establishes spacetime geometry and applies it to black holes, gravitational waves, and cosmology.
syllabus_topics: Review of Special Relativity and flat spacetime metric
Differential geometry: manifolds, connections, curvature tensor
Derivation of the Einstein Field Equations
The Schwarzschild solution: black holes and solar system tests
Introduction to gravitational radiation and Friedmann cosmology
textbooks: Spacetime and Geometry: An Introduction to General Relativity by Sean Carroll
Gravity: An Introduction to Einstein's General Relativity by James B. Hartle
relevance: The core course for studying gravity manipulation. Teaches how to formulate spacetime metrics, calculate energy conditions, and analyze warp metrics like the Alcubierre drive.

title: Advanced Aerospace Propulsion
subject: Aerospace Engineering
description: Analyzes the physics and engineering of air-breathing and rocket propulsion. Covers gas turbines, ramjets, scramjets, chemical rockets, and electric propulsion technologies.
syllabus_topics: Thermodynamic cycle analysis of turbojets and turbofans
Combustion physics, gas turbine components, and inlets
Chemical rocket dynamics, specific impulse, and nozzles
Electric propulsion: ion thrusters, Hall thrusters, and MPD thrusters
Advanced concept propulsion (fusion, sails, warp-metrics overview)
textbooks: Mechanics and Thermodynamics of Propulsion by Philip Hill & Carl Peterson
Rocket Propulsion Elements by George Sutton & Oscar Biblarz
relevance: Explores actual physical propulsion systems and provides a baseline for comparing classical chemical/electric rocket efficiency against theoretical space-bending warp drives.
